title: The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood

author.name: Howard Pyle
author.biography: Born in Wilmington, Delaware, he wrote and illustrated his own books and taught illustration to students such as N. C. Wyeth.

hook.text: Why would a whole countryside love a band of outlaws?

paragraphs: In the days of King Henry the Second, an eighteen-year-old archer sets out from Locksley for a shooting match at Nottingham. Before the day is over he has killed one of the King's foresters in a quarrel, and there is a reward of two hundred pounds on his head. He takes to Sherwood Forest, and other men join him there.

Many chapters start the same way: Robin, or one of his band, meets a stranger on the road, and they test each other with quarterstaffs, swords, bows or wits. Often the stranger ends up joining them, which is how Little John, Will Scarlet, Friar Tuck and others come to the greenwood.

Their great opponent is the Sheriff of Nottingham, who tries tricks, rewards and armed men, and is outwitted again and again. The outlaws take from rich travellers who can spare it and help people in trouble: a knight whose castle and lands are pledged for a debt to a grasping priory, a young man about to lose the woman he loves to a rich old knight.

Howard Pyle stitched the old Robin Hood ballads into one story, full of feasts, songs, disguises and May mornings. He opens by warning readers who cannot spare a moment for laughter to close the book at once.

orientation.text: Twenty-one adventures between a preface and an epilogue. Each chapter is a complete episode, and together they follow one story in order. The narrator often speaks to the reader directly, and the outlaws break into song.
